title: Minimum Replacements to Reduce Integer to One
description: Given a positive integer `n`, you can repeatedly apply one operation: if `n` is even, replace `n` with `n / 2`; if `n` is odd, replace `n` with either `n + 1` or `n - 1`. Return the minimum number of operations needed for `n` to become `1`.
hints: When `n` is odd, examine its lowest two bits (`n & 3`): if `(n & 3) == 1` or `n == 3`, decrementing produces more trailing zeros (or reaches 2 directly); otherwise incrementing creates at least two trailing zeros.
Promote `n` to a 64-bit integer so that adding 1 to `2^31 - 1` does not overflow a signed 32-bit integer.
